title: Steward-owned charter facilitation and addressable charter decisions
description:
Make vision-charter facilitation a steward-owned capability of the jit-project-lead skill and make charter decisions addressable items, so vision deliberation lands in the durable charter and every decision becomes a citable, machine-validated anchor.

## Background

The jit-project-lead steward owns a per-strategic-container vision charter (vision statement plus an append-only `D-N` decision log) but currently has no mode that facilitates creating it with the owner. Mode 3 (steering discussion) delegates to jit-planning-lead, whose interview machinery converges on container success criteria and plan documents and has no charter concept, so deliberation outcomes never reach the charter. Mode 2 (cold-start goal) has the same seam: the charter only materializes at first mode-1 dispatch, after planning is already done.

Comparable systems resolve this with a steward-owned facilitation step writing directly to the durable vision artifact. cc-sdd maintains steering documents through a dedicated command with two postures — bootstrap (derive a draft from repository state, then human ratification) and sync (drift detection with additive updates). BMAD's product-brief skill is the elicitation variant: a coached conversation that records every decision to a canonical decision log as it unfolds.

On the addressability side, the `definition` item kind is the proven precedent: a project-scope, markdown-first kind sourced from a repository markdown file, indexed by the same section-scanning path as issue descriptions. The extractor indexes bullet list entries under the kind's configured section that match its id-pattern; `###` headings do not index. The charter's decision log can plug into the same machinery once its format carries one summary bullet per decision.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: jit-project-lead mode 3 runs a steward-owned charter facilitation body; mode routing no longer hands steering discussions to jit-planning-lead.
- [hard] REQ-02: The facilitation body supports both entry postures — coached elicitation with the owner when the vision is unstated, and bootstrap from repository state (issues, containers, code) with owner ratification when project artifacts already exist — and selects the posture from the entry state.
- [hard] REQ-03: Every facilitation outcome lands in the charter as vision text or a new append-only `D-N` entry recording chosen, rejected, and reasoning; landed entries are superseded by new entries that cite them, never edited.
- [hard] REQ-04: Mode 2 runs the same charter step before handing the scoped goal to jit-planning-lead, so a cold start produces a charter before planning begins.
- [hard] REQ-05: The charter format holds one summary bullet per decision under `## Decision Log` (the addressable row, `- D-N: <one-liner>`) with the full entry under a following `## Decision Details` section; the skill's charter reference and template prescribe this shape.
- [hard] REQ-06: A project-scope, markdown-first `charter` item kind is declared over the charter document; `@/charter/D-N` resolves to the decision's summary row and `jit item list --kind charter` enumerates all logged decisions.
- [hard] REQ-07: A `per:@/charter/D-N` label on an issue resolves through link-label validation, and a dangling charter reference fails validation.
- [hard] REQ-08: The v1.0 charter exists at its config-derived permanent path with a ratified vision and seeded `D-N` entries for consequential decisions already made, and is doc-linked to the v1.0 strategic container.

## Notes

Decisions pinned during intake:

- **Kind name `charter`** (`@/charter/D-7`). Rejected: `charter-decision` with `cd` alias — longer with no resolution gain; `vision` — names the artifact's purpose rather than the document holding the log.
- **Link namespace: reuse `per`.** The issue-scope `decision` kind already declares it, and resolution is by qualified id, so issue-scope and charter decisions share it without ambiguity. Rejected: a new dedicated namespace — adds a registry entry for no disambiguation benefit.
- **Format: bullet index plus detail sections.** Rejected: single section with nested field bullets — item text quality would depend on parser nesting behavior instead of an authored one-liner.
- **Scope: single self-contained issue including full dogfooding** (skill body, template/reference updates, repo-local config kind, and the authored v1.0 charter). Rejected: a breakable container with its own plan bracket, and a two-sibling split — the charter format and the item kind must agree, so they land together.
- **Single static source accepted.** An item kind reads one config-declared source path, while charter paths embed the container short id. With one anchor-tier container this is fine as repo-local configuration; multi-source kinds for multiple concurrent charters are out of scope (a future product enhancement if ever needed).
